posts.title: FG, SG or AG: Choosing the Right Stud Type
posts.author: {{shortName}} Team
posts.excerpt: The wrong soleplate costs you grip, speed and comfort. Here's how to match your boots to the surface you actually play on.
body: Firm-ground (FG) boots are built for dry natural grass. Their moulded studs give explosive traction without sinking too deep into the turf.
Soft-ground (SG) boots use fewer, longer — often metal — studs that bite into wet, muddy pitches where FG studs would slip.
Artificial-grass (AG) boots have a high count of short, rounded studs that spread pressure evenly across 3G and 4G surfaces, reducing strain on your joints.

posts.title: Five Habits That Double Your Boots' Lifespan
posts.author: {{shortName}} Team
posts.excerpt: A few minutes after every session keeps your boots feeling match-ready for seasons, not months.
body: Knock off mud while it's still wet, then wipe the upper with a damp cloth. Never use a dishwasher or washing machine.
Stuff your boots with newspaper and let them dry at room temperature — radiators and direct sunlight crack leather and warp soleplates.
Rotate between two pairs if you train often, and always loosen the laces fully before taking them off.

posts.title: How to Break In New Boots Without the Blisters
posts.author: {{shortName}} Team
posts.excerpt: New boots should feel snug, not painful. Ease them in gradually and they'll mould to your feet.
body: Start by wearing your new boots around the house for an hour or two with match socks on.
Next, use them for light training sessions before trusting them for a full ninety minutes.
If a hot spot appears, tape the area early — prevention is far easier than treating a blister mid-season.
